parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent: start up FWKO V-001 per procedure with the bypass opened. Deviation (Start/Stop Procedures, Error guideword): start-up without opening the bypass (CASE-02 to CASE-04). Frequency C (Casual): omission of a single step during a non-routine but recurring task is credible over the unit life. The only safeguard is an administrative commissioning procedure (CASE-06) and no engineered barriers are listed, so B would require more credit than the procedure alone warrants. E (Frequent) is unsupported because start-ups are intermittent, a written procedure exists, and the consequence is only 'possible'. Severity II (Moderate): the stated consequence is internal damage to V-001 and accessories (CASE-05), confined to equipment in this node, with no stated loss of containment, injury, fire, or environmental release. III is plausible if repair needs an extended vessel outage; V (Catastrophic) is not supported. Matrix: II/C -> M, and III/C and III/B also give M. The preliminary E/V/H is rejected because it assumes repeated occurrence and catastrophic escalation not evidenced in the packet. Recommendations: make bypass opening an explicit, checklisted, signed-off step in the routine start-up procedure (not only commissioning); include it in operator training; and evaluate engineered measures such as bypass valve position indication or a start-up permissive, plus verification of internals design for start-up loads. Subjective probability (judgment aid only): about 20% that the stated damage occurs at least once over the unit life.
safeguards_considered: Existing: commissioning procedure (CASE-06). Administrative only; credited modestly in holding frequency at C rather than higher. Its effectiveness depends on being applied at every start-up, not only initial commissioning.
Not credited: the packet lists no alarms, interlocks, valve position indication, differential-pressure monitoring, or relief devices.
Recommended (not existing): an explicit bypass-opening step with checklist and sign-off in the routine start-up operating procedure.
Recommended (not existing): operator training and pre-start-up briefing on the FWKO start-up sequence and the consequences of omitting bypass opening.

Recommended for evaluation (not existing): bypass valve position indication or a start-up permissive, and verification that V-001 internals and accessories are designed for start-up surge and differential loads.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Node scope is limited to V-001 and associated lines, so consequences were evaluated within this node only.
The Start/Stop Procedures element with the Error guideword identifies a human-error deviation during a non-routine operating phase, which informs the frequency judgment.
The deviation is an error in start-up procedures, an intermittent task rather than a continuous-operation condition, which argues against Frequent (E).
The cause is omission of a single step (bypass not opened), a credible human error with no listed engineered barrier, supporting Casual (C) rather than a lower category.

The consequence is only possible internal damage to V-001 and accessories, with no stated loss of containment, injury, fire, or environmental impact. This supports Severity II and contradicts Catastrophic (V).
The only safeguard is an administrative commissioning procedure, credited modestly; its applicability to routine restarts is unverified.
Severity II x Frequency C gives M. Sensitivity: II/B gives L; III/B and III/C give M. H would require III/E, IV/D-E, or V/C-E, none of which is supported by the packet.

uncertainty_notes: The packet gives only category names, not descriptive or numerical criteria for frequency or severity. Assignments rely on conventional interpretation of the labels.

Start-up frequency and operator training are not stated. The packet also does not say whether the commissioning procedure governs routine restarts or only initial commissioning; if it covers only the first start-up, its credit for later restarts is lower.

The damage mechanism (e.g., surge or differential load on internals) and the bypass configuration are not described. The packet states no overpressure, loss of containment, injury, fire, or environmental release; if such escalation were credible, severity would need re-evaluation, potentially to IV.
No incident history, instrumentation, alarms, interlocks, or relief devices are listed, so none were credited.
Reasonable alternative ratings are B/II -> L, C/III -> M, and B/III -> M. M is judged most defensible, but L cannot be excluded.

The subjective probability of about 20% (that the stated internal damage occurs at least once over the unit's operating life) is a labeled judgment aid only. It is not derived from the qualitative matrix and does not rest on packet data.

You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence.   Severity I: A->L, B->L, C->L, D->M, E->M

A senior engineer has provided a preliminary estimate of frequency category E, severity category V, and High risk. Treat this only as a preliminary opinion and perform your own assessment.

# Independent judgment
Assign the frequency, severity, and qualitative risk categories independently.
